mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in WORKPLACES mobility indicates more people commuting to offices and workplaces, which increases weekday foot traffic and spending at retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES mobility continues to rise over the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility crosses above -50 percent, it signals that authorities have relaxed movement restrictions enough to restore public transit use, which precedes a broader reopening of retail and recreation sectors and lifts RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -50 percent in a weekly mean
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -50 but RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days does not exceed its level in the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility reflects a coordinated return of commuting and public movement; their interaction creates a stronger rebound in retail and recreation footfall than either alone, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than when only one of them rises.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates that households have shifted from panic buying to routine shopping, reducing stockpiling and freeing up trips for discretionary retail and recreation, which raises RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: If in a reopening regime GROCERY_PHARM mobility rises while RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: A steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility means people are spending less time at home and more time out in public, which directly increases visits to retail and recreation locations and drives RETAIL_REC upward.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to fall over the next week but RETAIL_REC over the following 7 days does not exceed its level in the previous 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 14 percent above baseline, it indicates that a sufficient share of the population has resumed out-of-home routines, triggering a sustained increase in retail and recreation visits and lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 14 percent above baseline
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL is below 14 and RETAIL_REC over the following 7 days is not higher than over the preceding 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising GROCERY_PHARM and rising TRANSIT mobility signals a broad normalization of daily travel and shopping patterns; together they amplify retail and recreation activity, driving RETAIL_REC up over four weeks.
failure_condition: If both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT rise but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of reopening and transit recovery, a continued rise in TRANSIT mobility reflects the removal of capacity limits on public transport, which spills over into greater retail and recreation mobility and raises RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues to rise in a reopening regime but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed its previous 28-day mean.
